title: Apricot and Almond Stuffed French Toast
changes_from_base: Cream cheese beaten with apricot jam and a drop of almond flavouring fills each sandwich; the bread goes through a thin egg, flour and water batter instead of the cinnamon milk custard.
summary: Golden fried sandwiches filled with a fruity apricot cream cheese and a hint of almond, lovely with a drizzle of syrup.

ingredients.item: slices good white sandwich bread (about 280 g)

steps.title: Combine filling
steps.text: Beat 113 g cream cheese with 1 tbsp caster sugar, 2 tbsp apricot jam and ⅛ tsp almond flavouring until completely smooth.

steps.title: Layer sandwiches
steps.text: Spread the filling onto 4 slices of bread and cover each with a second slice, pressing to seal.

steps.title: Make batter
steps.text: Whisk 1 egg, 240 ml cold water, 65 g plain flour and 1 tsp vanilla together in a shallow dish.

steps.title: Cook
steps.text: Melt half of the 56 g butter in a large non-stick pan, dunk two sandwiches briefly so the batter clings lightly, and fry until golden on both sides, around 3 min per side.

steps.title: Finish cooking
steps.text: Melt the remaining butter and fry the other two sandwiches in the same way.

steps.title: Serve warm
steps.text: Cut into triangles and serve at once, drizzled with 60 ml maple syrup.

tips: Beat the apricot jam into the softened cream cheese until smooth so the filling stays put and does not leak into the pan.
Dip the sandwiches quickly rather than soaking them, so the bread doesn't turn soggy.
A steady, warm pan keeps the crust crisp while the filling softens inside.
safety: Check the almond flavouring label if cooking for anyone with a nut allergy.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Enjoy right away for the crispest result; cover and refrigerate leftovers for up to a day, then reheat gently in a pan. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
